classification.difficultyReason: Select and explain the violated fitting criterion in each diagram: trend direction, straightness, observed range, or balance of points around the line.

content.prompt: Explain why these are not lines of best fit.

spec.description: Seven falling red crosses and an upward blue candidate line; unnumbered axes.
spec.mathematics: The candidate has the opposite direction from the data trend.
spec.answerVisibility: Candidate line is a permanent given; explanation is answer-only.

answer.short: It does not fit the data: the line rises while the data trend downwards.
answer.worked: The observations show a negative association, but the supplied line has a positive gradient. A line of best fit should follow the downward trend.

spec.description: Seven red crosses linked by a blue zigzag path on unnumbered axes.
spec.mathematics: Joining the points produces a broken path rather than one straight best-fit line.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied path remains visible; explanation is answer-only.

answer.short: A line of best fit is a single straight line.
answer.worked: The blue path changes direction as it joins the observations. A line of best fit should be one straight line through the middle of the distribution.

spec.description: Seven red crosses and a blue descending line extending beyond them at both ends.
spec.mathematics: The supplied segment extends outside the observed horizontal range.
spec.answerVisibility: Candidate line is permanent; explanation is answer-only.

answer.short: The line extends past the data.
answer.worked: The line continues beyond the first and last observations. For this by-eye sketch, keep the line within the observed range because the relationship may not continue outside it.

spec.description: Nineteen orange observations on a unit grid with labelled arrowed axes; green descending candidate line.
spec.mathematics: Observation coordinates are supplied by the inventory. Candidate endpoints reproduce visual placement approximately; more points are below the line.
spec.answerVisibility: Green line is a permanent given; explanation is answer-only.

answer.short: Too many data points are below the line.
answer.worked: Most observations lie below the supplied line. Move the line lower so that it is closer to the observations and has roughly equal numbers of points above and below.

spec.description: Same nineteen orange observations on a unit grid; green horizontal candidate line slightly above y=5.
spec.mathematics: The exact candidate height is not stated; 5.25 is a graphic reconstruction, not a numerical given. The candidate ignores the downward trend.
spec.answerVisibility: Green line is a permanent given; explanation is answer-only.

answer.short: It does not fit the data: the data trend downwards, but the line is horizontal.
answer.worked: The observations show a negative association. A horizontal line does not follow that trend; the line of best fit should slope downwards through the middle of the observations.
